title: Bank of England MPC decision — the last 2026 meeting, and the thinnest document set of the three (12:00 London / 07:00 ET; no Monetary Policy Report)
source: EST: bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the 2026 announcement table runs 'Thursday 5 February' through 'Thursday 17 December', and the 17 December row links ONLY 'December MPC Summary and minutes' with no Monetary Policy Report (the 2026 MPR months are February, April, July and November). The same fetch returns the 2027 PROVISIONAL list, 'Thursday 4 February' through 'Thursday 16 December'. UPGRADED THIS SESSION FROM A SECOND BoE PRIMARY the proposal did not have: bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy-summary-and-minutes/2026/december-2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200), is already live and states the minutes 'will be published on 17 December 2026' under a page title carrying '(to be published at 12pm)' — so the 12:00 London clock is now the Bank's own, not press convention. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has FED: and no slot for a non-Fed central bank — the same gap boe-decision-2026-09-17, boe-decision-2026-11-05, ecb-decision-2026-09-10 and boj-decision-2026-09-18 were filed under. The DATE is the Bank's own; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/boe-decision-2026-12-17.from-boe-decision-2026-11-05.json (read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). That proposal's placement finding stands and is kept: December is the conditional half of one two-meeting question, and the scoring venue for the sibling lane's FT-boe-decision-2026-09-17-3. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDED, AND IT RE-FRAMES BOTH SIBLINGS. (1) THE STRIP DECOMPOSES. centralbank.watch's implied rate reproduces exactly from its own probabilities on the two near meetings (3.75 + 0.069x0.25 = 3.77; 3.75 + 0.542x0.25 = 3.89), so the same construction solves December's 94.6%-higher / 4.11% implied into a three-outcome distribution: NO hike 5.4%, exactly one 45.2%, two 49.4%. Two consequences. P(Bank Rate at or below 4.00% after 12-17) is about 50.6% (48.6-52.6% across the implied-rate rounding band) — the sibling's FT-boe-decision-2026-09-17-3 is a COIN FLIP against the strip, not the contrarian under its framing implies. And P(hike at December | November holds) = (45.8-5.4)/45.8 = 88.2% — so FT-boe-decision-2026-11-05-1 passing CONCENTRATES the December residual rather than relieving it. (2) DECEMBER, NOT NOVEMBER, IS WHERE THE STRIP-VS-SURVEY DISAGREEMENT IS ADJUDICATED: November's 54.2% is a coin flip both camps survive; December's 94.6%-higher against a Reuters panel at 87.5%-no-change-in-2026 (13-18 Aug, 64 economists) and the Bank's own Market Participants Survey end-2026 median of 3.75% (15-17 Jul, 78 respondents) is an ~82-point gap one side must be flatly wrong about. (3) THE STALENESS OBJECTION HAS A SHARPER DATE THAN THE GILT BLOW-OUT: both surveys also close BEFORE Warsh's 2026-08-28 Jackson Hole keynote, which took Fed September hike odds 35.4% -> 57.5% in one session and left the Dec-9 FOMC pricing no cut branch at all (fomc-2026-12-09 ledger). The UK strip's December number is partly an imported global repricing; the MPC votes on UK data. (4) MEASURED PRECEDENT THAT THIS STRIP OVER-PRICES UK TIGHTENING: in March 2026 the same market briefly priced FOUR BoE hikes for 2026 against a pre-conflict two-CUT baseline; none has been delivered. (5) THE PAYLOAD IS THE THINNEST OF THE THREE MEETINGS: September carried an unpriced annual QT review, November carries a forecast round, December publishes summary + minutes + vote and nothing else — maximum priced conviction, minimum published reasoning, and the next MPR is 2027-02-04. THE RUN-IN IS ONE DAY: UK CPI for November data publishes 2026-12-16 07:00 London (ONS release page, fetched direct 2026-09-09, 'not yet published') — proposed to the calendar in this PR. The December UK labour-market date is NOT yet announced (gov.uk statistics announcements, fetched 2026-09-09: zero results in the December-2026 window) and is deliberately NOT proposed. ATTRIBUTION IS THE WORST OF ANY BoE ENTRY: 23 tracked events sit within five days, including ecb-decision-2026-12-17 THE SAME DAY at 14:15 CET / 08:15 ET — 75 minutes after this one, also pre-open, and carrying a staff projection round the BoE does not have — plus boj-decision-2026-12-18, opex-2026-12-18 (quarterly), retail-sales-2026-12-16 and fomc-2026-12-09 eight days prior. Tiered medium to match the September and November entries; NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED: symbols: [], no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed.
